findings.summary: crates/server/src/board.rs:66: pr_for picks with `max_by_key(|p| p.by_branch)`, and on a tie `max_by_key` returns the last match. GitHub lists PRs newest first, so the last match is the oldest PR. When two open PRs' branches both name a ticket (a re-opened PR, or a split such as backend/tru-6-a and backend/tru-6-b), or when two PRs tie only by title, the card and the Needs you 'merge' item show the oldest one and drop the rest without a log line. crates/server/tests/github.rs only tests one PR per ticket on a branch that names it against one tied by title, so no test covers this tie.
findings.reason: Ties now go to the highest PR number, the newest.

findings.summary: crates/server/src/github.rs:97: checks() reads only check-runs and counts zero runs as Pending. A PR whose CI reports through commit statuses, or that has no Actions runs, shows 'checks pending' forever and never gets a 'merge' item in Needs you. Still open from Build rounds 1 and 2 and from Verify round 2.

crates/server/src/github.rs:63-64: each per-PR check-runs and contents call ends in `?`. A single 403 or 5xx on one PR fails the whole GitHub read, and every repo keeps its stale PR list. The pulls call at :56 and the check-runs call at :63 read only the first page (per_page=100), and nothing is logged when more pages exist. Still open from Build rounds 1 and 2.
